To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we can successfully train a neural network with 2 billion parameters on 1,024 GPUs; 2) the LBANN toolkit is highly scalable; and 3) LBANN can achieve 3.4 petaFLOPS of peak performance on a single GPU node.
the LBANN toolkit has demonstrated the ability to train a model with 1.3 billion parameters using 1,152 GPUs.

LBANN can scale to 16,384 NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs and train a model with 3.2 trillion weights in 3.3 minutes, and that LBANN can scale beyond 16,384 GPUs and train a 4.4 trillion weight model in less than 5 minutes.

developing and evaluating the LBANN toolkit to train large scale neural network models on HPC systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to train a model of 1.6B weights on 1,280 nodes (25,600 CPU cores) in 3 hours and 40 minutes.
we have been able to scale a model to a 1.3 billion parameter model on a 10,000 core system, and a 1.5 billion parameter model on 12,000 cores.
we have been able to scale the size of neural network models to 2.4 billion parameters, and we are working to scale to 10 billion parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HPC resources are capable of training neural networks that are orders of magnitudes larger than those that can be trained by the current state-of-the-art deep learning frameworks.
the LBANN toolkit can train models with over 1 billion parameters on 100s of GPUs.
HPC systems can be leveraged to significantly increase the size and complexity of deep neural networks that can be trained, which will enable new scientific and commercial applications.
